problem:
Title: Probability Generating Function defines Probability Distribution

Let $X$ and $Y$ be [[Definition:Discrete Random Variable|discrete random variables]]  whose [[Definition:Codomain of Mapping|codomain]], $\Omega_X$, is a [[Definition:Subset|subset]] of the [[Definition:Natural Numbers|natural numbers]] $\N$.

Let the [[Definition:Probability Generating Function|probability generating functions]] of $X$ and $Y$ be $\map {\Pi_X} s$ and $\map {\Pi_Y} s$ respectively.

Then:
:$\forall s \in \closedint {-1} 1: \map {\Pi_X} s = \map {\Pi_Y} s$
{{iff}}:
:$\forall k \in \N: \Pr \left({X = k}\right) = \map \Pr {Y = k}$

That is, [[Definition:Discrete Random Variable|discrete random variables]] which are [[Definition:Integer|integer-valued]] have the same [[Definition:Probability Generating Function|PGFs]] {{iff}} they have the same [[Definition:Probability Mass Function|PMF]].
